'''Dak Ralter''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] and [[Gunner/Legends|gunner]] of [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Group]], who served the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. He was [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker's]] aerial gunner during the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], where he was [[Death/Legends|killed]].

==Biography==
===Early life and escape to freedom===
{{Quote|I had a good teacher.|Dak Ralter, referring to [[Breg]], when asked about his natural piloting and gunnery talents|<ref name="GG3" />}}
[[Dak Ralter's parents]] were children of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], who greatly valued the peace and prosperity of those days, and later became [[Politics/Legends|political]] prisoners in the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Kalist Base|labor colony]] on [[Kalist VI/Legends|Kalist VI]]. Born to prisoners into captivity, Ralter instead only knew [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] as a place of fear, oppression, and the Empire. As a youth, his parents would often model his dreams with tales of the wonder and delight that existed before the [[Declaration of a New Order|formation of the Empire]]. These stories were about all that kept him going during his days living inside the huge [[Transparisteel/Legends|transparisteel]] dome of Kalist VI.<ref name="GG3" /><ref name="RS guide" />

His parents' stories helped to keep alive a spark of hope inside the young Ralter. He knew that someday his hopes would come to fruition, as they did when he was seventeen standard years old. A new prisoner named [[Breg]] came to the camp one day, and being just a bit older than Ralter, the two became fast friends. Breg was a [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] who was downed while on a reconnaissance mission. Luckily for Breg, the Empire did not know of his affiliation, or he likely would have faced an [[Interrogation droid/Legends|interrogation droid]], or worse.<ref name="GG3" />

Breg was a free spirit who fueled the flame of liberty inside of Ralter with further tales of a life beyond the confines of Kalist VI. He made quite an impact on the impressionable Ralter. Together they planned an escape from the penal colony. Ralter took to this opportunity with all the energy born of a lifetime of pent-up anger and aggression. When his parents learned of their son's plan, they encouraged him, knowing it might be his only chance for a life beyond captivity. They also knew that trying to go with him would only hamper his chances, and they insisted he go without them. It was a difficult choice for the teenage Ralter, but he heeded their wishes.<ref name="GG3" />

Their plan was to hijack an [[Imperial prison barge]] and blast away from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]]. While waiting for the barge, Breg and Ralter vaulted the inner power fence of the camp, shorted out the outer fence, and managed to make it past the unsuspecting sentries. Once a few slightly-used Imperial guard uniforms were "borrowed," gaining access to the landing area was relatively easy. They triggered a false reactor alarm and staged a prearranged power outage in order to board the prison barge and clear all moorings. But before they could lift off, an Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]] saw what was happening, boarded the ship, and tried to stop the two youths. Breg was shot before Ralter could blast the [[Troop/Legends|trooper]] in return. The Rebel fugitive lay wounded and dying on the cockpit floor.<ref name="GG3" />

This left the piloting duties up to Ralter. He had no previous experience with any technology more sophisticated than a [[Laser/Legends|laser]] drill. He bravely manned the [[Starship/Legends|ship's]] controls while Breg, only able to speak, directed him through takeoff. Ralter displayed a natural affinity for flying. Under Breg's guidance they were able to blast away from the planet and escape into [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]. Breg instructed Ralter to plot a course for the [[Tierfon Rebel Outpost|Rebel base]] on the planet [[Tierfon/Legends|Tierfon]]. When they arrived, Ralter was forced to land the ship unaided. Breg's condition had worsened and he now lay unconscious. The landing was by no means pretty, but it was in many respects miraculous. Despite the best efforts of Ralter to save his friend, Breg died soon after landing. Nevertheless, with Breg's help Ralter was able to escape imprisonment and start a new life with the Rebel Alliance.<ref name="GG3" />

===Serving the Rebellion===
To honor the man responsible for his freedom, Ralter joined the Rebellion's pilot corps, completing his training as a [[Tierfon Yellow Aces/Legends|Tierfon Yellow Ace]].<ref name="EGTW" /><ref name="GG3" /> After proving his piloting abilities, he was assigned to the burgeoning [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Flight]]<ref name="RS/RF" /> under the command of [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. Officially, Ralter replaced [[Biggs Darklighter/Legends|Biggs Darklighter's]] spot in the [[Squadron/Legends|squadron]]. He was one of the youngest pilots to serve with the group during his tenure.<ref name="RS">[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']]</ref>

His earliest service with the Rogues saw him escorting convoys through Imperial territory and participating in some of the squadron's most dangerous early conflicts. He assisted in [[Rendezvous on Barkhesh|protecting]] supply convoys against Imperial forces on the planet [[Barkhesh/Legends|Barkhesh]]; [[Search for the Nonnah|recovering]] the downed Rebel ship, the ''[[Nonnah]]'', on [[Chorax]]; the [[Battle of Corellia (1 ABY)|evacuation]] of General [[Crix Madine/Legends|Crix Madine]] from the Imperial assault on [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]]; the [[Liberation of Gerrard V|liberation]] of [[Gerrard V]]; the [[Battle of the Jade Moon|destruction]] of Imperial installations on the [[Jade Moon]] of [[Loronar/Legends|Loronar]]; [[Raid on Balmorra|destruction]] of the [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|AT-AT]] manufacturing facility on [[Balmorra/Legends|Balmorra]]; the [[Assault on Kile II|destruction]] of the [[Kile II]] [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]]; and the [[Rescue on Kessel|rescue]] of [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] from the penal colony of [[Kessel/Legends|Kessel]]. In [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]], he fought in the campaign against [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Kohl Seerdon]], including service at the [[Battle above Taloraan]], the [[Escape from Fest]], Seerdon's [[blockade on Chandrila]], the [[Raid on Sullust]], and the ultimate destruction of Seerdon during his [[Attack on Thyferra|invasion]] of the [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]] facilities on [[Thyferra/Legends|Thyferra]].<ref name="RS" />

Also in 1 ABY, he was seen in [[Dearic/Legends|Dearic]] on the planet [[Talus/Legends|Talus]].<ref name="Star Wars Galaxies">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref>

===Battle of Hoth and death===
{{Quote|Dak? Dak!|Luke Skywalker, after Dak's death|<ref name="ESB" />}}
[[File:Dak-hd.png|thumb|left|250px|Ralter, in the gunner's seat of a [[Snowspeeder/Legends|snowspeeder]] during the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]].]]
When the [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]] moved their operations to the newly established [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] on the planet [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] in [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]], Ralter was assigned there with the rest of the Rogues. He flew with Rogue Group during the Imperial [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|invasion]] of the planet, serving as Rogue Leader's [[Gunner/Legends|gunner]] in the rear of his [[Snowspeeder/Legends|snowspeeder]].<ref name="SWCVD">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> It was the responsibility of the Rogues to hold off the Imperial advance long enough to buy time for the highly vulnerable [[Transport/Legends|transports]] carrying vital equipment and personnel to evacuate the planet, and Ralter's gunnery skills paired with Skywalker's flying abilities proved deadly to several enemies.<ref name="RS" /> Eventually, Skywalker prepared to make the first attack run on the line of AT-AT [[Walker/Legends|walkers]], and he ordered Ralter to use the [[Airspeeder/Legends|speeder's]] [[Power harpoon launcher|harpoon and tow cable]] to trip the massive war machine. However, the speeder's aft section took a direct hit from an AT-AT's powerful laser barrage, killing Ralter instantly. Any chance of recovering Ralter's body was then lost when the speeder was crushed under the massive footpad of one of the advancing AT-ATs, after Skywalker was shot down.<ref name="GG3" /><ref name="ESB" />

===Legacy===
Ralter's death stayed with Skywalker. In [[19 ABY/Legends|19 ABY]], he thought about Ralter, along with several of his other comrades who perished in action, upon seeing the young [[Qom Jha and Qom Qae|Qom Qae]] [[Child Of Winds]]' enthusiasm for battle.<ref name="VOTF">''[[Vision of the Future]]''</ref>

==Personality and traits==
Born inside Kalist VI's transparisteel enclosure, the only understanding Ralter had of the outside world was what his parents and fellow prisoners told him of their past life, and what new information he could cobble together from the newly imprisoned. In an environment populated by those unjustly held by the Empire, it was only natural that a great sense of anger and anxiety developed within the youth.<ref name="GG3" />

[[File:LukeDakEchoBase-TESB40.png|thumb|right|250px|Dak expresses his enthusiasm to face the Empire to Skywalker.]]
To say Ralter was overly-enthusiastic with a longing for excitement and a chance to take on the Empire would be an understatement. He still strongly exuded these tendencies by the time he was transferred to Echo Base on Hoth, even after nearly three years of service to the Rebellion. In his first days with Rogue Group, his exuberance was likened to that of a young Luke Skywalker.<ref name="GG3" /><ref name="ESB" /> Skywalker saw something of himself in him.<ref name="RS guide">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron: The Official Nintendo Player's Guide]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Dak_GG3_1stEd.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Dak from ''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]'']]
Dak Ralter was portrayed by [[John Morton]] in the [[1980]] movie [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''The Empire Strikes Back'']], the second installment of the ''Star Wars'' [[Original trilogy]].<ref name="ESB" /> In the video game [[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']], Dak's voice is provided by [[Raphael Sbarge]].

The character's name appeared in the movie credits as "Dak (Luke's Gunner)," and "Dak" was used in the [[Star Wars home video releases|DVD]] subtitles.<ref name="ESB" /> However, many third party products and official resources released after the film, such as the [[StarWars.com]] [[Databank (original)|Databank]],<ref name="DB">{{DB|character|dackralter|Ralter, Dak}}</ref> the [[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back Cine-Manga|PhotoComic adaptation]]<ref name="Photocomic">[[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back Cine-Manga|''Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back'' Cine-Manga]]</ref> and ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''<ref name="CSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> showed Ralter's first name misspelled as "Dack,"<ref name="Photocomic" /> even well after [[Lucasfilm]] continuity expert [[Leland Chee]] went on the record to state that "Dak" was the accepted form.<ref name="SWF">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=158725&start=97#8047131|thread=Spelling Discrepancies|user=[[Leland Chee|Leland Y Chee]]|date=2004-09-27|time=10:18 AM|quote=The subtitles used in the DVDs provide great fuel for this discussion. For example, since the "Dak" spelling is what appears in both the credits and the subtitles of The Empire Strikes Back, moving forward, that's what we'll try to consistently go with for Luke's gunner instead of "Dack" Ralter.}}</ref> This naming was resolved with the 2012 release of ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'', where the character is correctly called "Dak."

Dak Ralter appeared in the [[2003]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'', a [[Wikipedia:Massively multiplayer online role-playing game|massively multiplayer online roleplaying game]] developed by [[Sony]] Online Entertainment and published by [[LucasArts]],<ref name="SWG:SK">{{GalaxiesNGE}}</ref> prior to its closure on [[December 15]], [[2011]].<ref name="Shutdown">{{SonyCite|url=playerinfo|text=IMPORTANT INFORMATION ABOUT ''STAR WARS'' GALAXIES™}}</ref> Dak Ralter was intended to be the Rebel quest giver for the fifth and final chapter of the story arc "[[W:c:swg:Secrets of the Syren|Secrets of the Syren]]". This chapter was achieving its development in [[October]] [[2005]]<ref name="ID">{{SonyCite|url=content.jsp?page=In%20Development|text=In Development}}</ref> but was delayed and planned to be introduced in [[April]] [[2006]] with the "[[W:c:swg:Publish 28 Notes for April 26, 2006|Publish 28]]."<ref name="P28">{{WebCite|url=https://forums.mmorpg.com/discussion/72650/pub-28-notes|text=Pub 28 Notes|date=2006-03-31|nobackup=1}}</ref> Dak Ralter and Officer [[Edgar]], the Imperial quest giver, were both added to the game with the Publish 28, released on [[April 26]], 2006.<ref name="SonyForumsCite-What's On Deck! Publish 28 Update Notes, April 26th">{{SonyForumsCite|url=swg/board/message?board.id=Announcements&message.id=3077&jump=true|text=What's On Deck! Publish 28 Update Notes, April 26th}}</ref> Nevertheless, the final chapter of "Secrets of the Syren" was never released and these NPCs did not provide any quest.<ref name="SWG:SK" />
